title: CrossLanguageValidation
description: Records the result of cross-referencing a KJV ScriptureRecord against the corresponding Original Hebrew, Greek, and/or Aramaic source texts. Produced by 'language_validator' subagents to confirm that the English translation faithfully preserves the original financial meaning and context.

validation_id.description: Globally unique identifier for this cross-language validation record (UUID v4).

schema_version.description: Semantic version of the CrossLanguageValidation schema (e.g. '1.0.0').

scripture_record_id.description: UUID of the ScriptureRecord (KJV English) that this validation pertains to.

english_reference.description: Human-readable Bible reference for the validated passage.

language_results.description: Validation results for each original language consulted.

source_text.description: The original-language text of the passage (rendered in its native script, e.g. Hebrew Unicode).

transliteration.description: Optional romanised transliteration of the original-language text.

key_terms.description: Financially significant terms found in this language's text.

original_term.description: The term as it appears in the original-language text.

strongs_number.description: Strong's Concordance reference number (e.g. 'H3701' for silver/money in Hebrew, 'G5536' for money/possessions in Greek).

english_gloss.description: Standard English gloss for this term (e.g. 'silver', 'money', 'debt').

financial_relevance.description: How directly this term relates to the financial theme: 'primary' terms explicitly denote financial concepts; 'secondary' terms have strong financial connotations; 'contextual' terms acquire financial meaning from surrounding text.

alignment_score.description: Numeric measure of how closely the KJV translation aligns with the original-language meaning (0.0 = no alignment, 1.0 = perfect alignment).

context_preserved.description: Whether the original linguistic and cultural context is adequately preserved in the English translation.

financial_theme_confirmed.description: Whether the financial theme is confirmed to be present in the original-language text (not an artifact of the English translation).

alignment_status.description: Qualitative assessment of the translation's fidelity to the original.

notes.description: Optional commentary from the language_validator agent explaining nuances, translation choices, or caveats.

source_corpus.description: Reference to the specific text corpus used (e.g. 'Westminster Leningrad Codex', 'NA28', 'Peshitta').

overall_status.description: Aggregate validation outcome across all languages. 'validated' requires all consulted languages to confirm the financial theme; 'partially_validated' means at least one language confirmed it; 'failed' means none confirmed it.

validated_by_agent.description: Identifier of the 'language_validator' agent instance that produced this record.

task_id.description: UUID of the AgentTask that generated this validation record.

validated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this validation was completed.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this record was created.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this record was last updated.

language_results.source_text: עָשִׁ֣יר בְּרָשִׁ֣ים יִמְשׁ֑וֹל וְעֶ֥בֶד לֹוֶ֗֝ה לְאִ֣ישׁ מַלְוֶֽה׃
language_results.transliteration: ashir b'rashim yimshol, v'eved loveh l'ish malveh
language_results.notes: The Hebrew terms for borrower (loveh) and lender (malveh) are unambiguous financial terms. The KJV rendering 'borrower is servant to the lender' faithfully preserves both meaning and tone.
